text:
ashley: Quick check — wiring up a private VPC endpoint to send telemetry to partner analytics. Two quick Qs:
1) Should we enable private DNS on the interface endpoint, or point an internal ALIAS to the endpoint ENIs?
2) For outbound to partner IPs, will traffic go via the VPC endpoint ENIs (so no NAT needed), or do we need NAT/egress path? Trying to avoid opening broad outbound NAT rules.

Here's the snippet I'm about to apply:
```hcl
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "partner" {
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.vpce.partner-analytics"
  vpc_id       = var.vpc_id
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  private_dns_enabled = true
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.vpce_sg.id]
}
```
Any concerns about conntrack, SGs, or logs containing partner IPs? tagging for egress/security review — thanks.

sam: If this is an interface endpoint, enabling private DNS is simpler — you get automatic DNS mapping to ENI IPs. No ALIAS needed unless you want explicit CNAME control. Traffic to the service endpoint will stay in-VPC to the ENIs, so you typically don't need NAT for that path. NAT is only for gateway-type endpoints (S3) or if you intentionally route outbound via IGW/NAT. Make sure the endpoint SG allows outbound 443 to partner, and your instances can talk to the endpoint SG's ENIs. Also check if partner requires mutual TLS or client certs.

priya: also watch conntrack on NAT/SG side — if you accidentally route via NAT, connection counts can spike. If you keep it via VPCE, SGs still matter: restrict outbound to partner CIDR and port 443. For logging: redact partner IPs in centralized logs (cloudtrail/flow logs) — we need a redaction rule in the logging pipeline. @sec-team can you confirm required redaction pattern?

sec-team: quick ack — from security POV: +1 to private DNS for simplicity. Approve config pending two things: (1) open a security-review ticket with the partner CIDR and threat model, (2) add a note about log redaction and retention. Also confirm the VPC endpoint policy limits actions to only 'Describe'/'Connect' as appropriate. We'll do a quick perms and egress audit once ticket exists. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: FYI conntrack note: if traffic is routed through NAT we saw high ephemeral port usage with 100k+ flows during test. Recommend testing with low-traffic smoke before rollout, and add monitoring for SNAT table saturation. Suggest using `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` bump if unavoidable.

ashley: Thanks all — will open CH-1234 with CIDR + logs redaction steps and tag @sec-team. Will keep private DNS enabled and lock SG to partner CIDR:443. I'll run a canary and report back. :thumbsup:
